subject: Vendor evaluation: economic & ops comparison for inference deployment (Helio)
messages:
From: Emma Li <emma@heliosys.com>
To: dylan_brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Helio vendor comparison - initial data and cost questions

Hi Dylan,

Thanks again for taking the time yesterday. We ran a quick internal scan and as we move toward a formal vendor decision we need a clearer line-item view of real unit economics and the uplift required to meet our SLA/throughput needs. Two specific asks to start: 

1) A concise comparison of run-rate unit cost at our forecasted 600M tokens/month across (a) Redwood hosted with standard batching, (b) Redwood Dedicated reserved pool, and (c) your hosted + KV-cache optimization assumptions.
2) Migration-related one-time friction: egress, onboarding engineering hours, and any model-compatibility tuning that Helio should budget for.

We already put together a CSV with what we’re using for Helio’s internal baseline (attached). Can your team confirm assumptions and call out where you’d need commercial concessions (credits, pilot discounts, onboarding waivers) to make the economics neutral vs. our incumbent?

Attachments: helio_comparison.csv (internal baseline)

We’d like to lock a short call after you send the line items — ideally Friday PST.

Thanks,
Emma Li
Corporate Procurement, Helio Systems

From: dylan_brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Li <emma@heliosys.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Helio vendor comparison - initial data and cost questions

Emma —

Appreciate the spreadsheet. I kicked this to Commercial and Engineering to get a crisp, line-by-line response. Quick notes up front to set expectations:

- Hosted vs Dedicated: Dedicated gives you predictable latency and better unit economics at volume (we can pick custom instance sizes to align with batch profiles), but it does require a short provisioning lead time.
- Migration friction is typically dominated by egress and integration work (network/certing, and any model/tokenization mismatches). We can offset some of that with onboarding credits and a time-boxed tuning engagement.

I’ll attach a commercial proposal sketch and a proposed mutual action plan in my next note. If Friday PST still works for a call, I’ll include Marissa for the commercial walkthrough and Connor for the technical Q&A.

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood_concession_matrix.xlsx (coming)

From: Emma Li <emma@heliosys.com>
To: dylan_brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: Helio Systems Procurement <procurement@heliosys.com>
Date: Thu, 13 May 2027 08:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Helio vendor comparison - initial data and cost questions

Thanks Dylan — received. I’ve added a sheet that maps our incumbent’s effective net rate (post-support credits) to the token consumption profile in the CSV. Attaching updated file from our side.

Quick clarifiers before Friday:
- Our incumbent has agreed a temporary 10% net rebate and a six-week onboarding credit. For us to progress we need a comparable or better commercial package plus clear proof points on latency at 99th percentile.
- We expect a deterministic plan for rollback in case integration hits unexpected ops friction.

Attachments: helio_comparison.csv (v2)

On the call we’ll bring our platform lead and SRE to validate ops assumptions.

Emma

From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Li <emma@heliosys.com>, dylan_brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: connor_obrien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 13 May 2027 10:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Proposed concession framework and run-rate math

Emma / Dylan —

I reviewed Helio’s baseline and sketched a concession matrix that preserves margin while addressing Helio’s immediate asks. High-level offer we can put on the table: 

- 3-month pilot: $50k credit applied to token usage (hosted) to match incumbent's short-term rebate.
- Dedicated reservation pricing: 12% off list at 600M tokens/mo equivalent if Helio commits to a 12-month reserved pool (includes automatic KV-cache tuning).
- Onboarding: waive up to $25k in migration engineering fees for a standard migration scope (network certs, tokenizers, and model validation).
- SLA: 99th percentile latency target with runbook and a 2-week rollback window; outage credits defined in SLA.

I attached the concession matrix and a worked example showing run-rate delta after credits and prepay. Key assumptions: Helio tolerates a 6–8 week Dedicated carveout timeline; any bespoke adapter work (non-standard tokenizers / custom model ops) will be scoped separately.

Attachments: redwood_concession_matrix.xlsx

Marissa Cole
Sr. Director, Commercial Solutions — Redwood Inference

From: connor_obrien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
To: dylan_brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Emma Li <emma@heliosys.com>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 08:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Technical integration notes and cost offsets

Emma / team —

Couple of pragmatic technical points to call out that change the cost calculus: 

1) Egress: if Helio elects Dedicated with co-located ingress, egress costs can be reduced by ~40% compared to a broad-hosted egress pattern. We’ll quantify in the run-rate sheet but wanted you to see it up front.
2) KV cache / prefix caching: a short 2-week tuning sprint typically yields 15–25% token reduction on chat-heavy workloads — we’ll include this in the Dedicated math.
3) Tokenization mismatches: if Helio uses a custom tokenizer, we’ll need a 1–2 week adapter dev sprint. If this happens it’s usually one-time effort (~40 engineer hours).

Suggested offset: convert a portion of pilot credit into a migration prepay that covers the tokenization adapter and the first month of egress to keep cash-neutral for Helio while giving us coverage for custom engineering.

I attached a short technical pack with a sample migration timeline and the minimal acceptance tests we run during cutover.

Attachments: technical-integration-notes.pdf

Connor O'Brien
Solutions Architect — Redwood Inference

From: Emma Li <emma@heliosys.com>
To: dylan_brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, connor_obrien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 17:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Vendor evaluation: economic & ops comparison for inference deployment (Helio)

Team —

Thanks for the fast turnaround and the detail. Helio’s procurement and SRE reviewed the concession matrix and technical notes. A few takeaways: 

- The 3-month $50k credit + $25k onboarding waiver is promising and addresses procurement’s short-term net-rate ask.
- We still need quantitative 99p latency numbers for the Dedicated configuration at 600M tokens/mo and an explicit rollback runbook (we’ll validate during the call).
- Procurement would prefer the migration prepay approach you suggested (convert $30k of pilot credit to prepay to cover adapter work + first month egress). That keeps accounting clean for us.

Can we lock a 45-minute call Monday (US/PST) to run the SLA numbers with SRE and close commercial terms? If so, please send the calendar invite and the final concession sheet ahead of the call.

Best,
Emma Li
Helio Systems — Corporate Procurement
